calls.video_title: 🚨MAJOR BUY: Last EASY Wealth Opportunity For Decades
calls.stated_price: No price target; forward P/E 56 -> 17, price-to-sales 3.5 -> 3.3
calls.thesis: New 'eight-year stock': revenue doubled in five years, operating income tripled (intro says quadrupled - captions inconsistent); forward P/E compressed 56 -> 17 and price-to-sales 3.5 -> 3.3 while AWS remains the best cloud provider; calls the sell-off a generational buying opportunity.
calls.base_case: Earnings keep growing and prices follow long term; S&P 500 forward P/E now 17 vs 23 a year ago and below the 10-year average of 19, while S&P earnings grow 32-33%.
calls.bull_case: AI capex cycle is just starting - cloud backlogs ~$2T, Google Cloud +103%, Azure +48%, AWS +40% - and the Fed eventually cuts as oil falls, unleashing compressed prices.

calls.video_title: What I'm Buying In The Most Disconnected Market I've Seen
calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (last BUY 24 Nov). Continuing to buy aggressively — deploying a record amount of capital in the sell-off. Amazon's price to operating cash flow is the lowest since 2010 while the business accelerates: company revenue growth 15%, AWS approaching 40% (fastest in 5 years), operating margins at all-time highs as AWS grows share of the mix. AWS capex has a ~3-year payback, then ~2 years of near-pure free cash flow; frontier AI labs are only ~7% of AWS revenue, demand is broad-based from tens of thousands of customers.
calls.base: AWS keeps compounding and the capex converts into free cash flow in the 2030s harvest phase.
calls.bull: The market recognises hyperscaler capex is paying off and multiples re-rate while growth accelerates.
calls.bear: The capex cycle suppresses free cash flow longer than expected, or AI demand slows.
calls.price_at_call: P/OCF lowest since 2010; AWS revenue growth approaching 40%

calls.thesis: Adding aggressively on Friday's >4% sell-off; AWS capex ~$220B in 2026 with ~20% ROIC and demand visibility into 2027-29; operating cash flow compounding ~31%/yr vs share price ~9%/yr since Q4 2021, P/OCF ~16.5x vs ~25x long-term median; 2nd-largest position, >15% of portfolio.

calls.video_title: The Stock Market Is Crashing - What I'm Doing Now
calls.thesis: Continuing to increase allocation; now a 15% position, his second-largest holding, and 'extremely bullish'. AWS flywheel: AI pulls core workloads into the cloud, growth accelerating across tens of thousands of customers; AWS AI is mostly durable inference, not training. Neocloud risk is localised, not systemic. Fundamentals growing far faster than the share price, multiples compressing.
calls.base_case: Companies keep using more compute and AI, and AWS is where they pay for it; durable growth for years.
calls.bull_case: Investors finally recognise AWS durability and the share price catches up to intrinsic value growth.
calls.bear_case: Market keeps pricing only next quarter and the share price keeps lagging intrinsic value.

calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY — he added to his Amazon position in after-hours trading after the Q3 print; Amazon remains his second-largest position. The ~7% after-hours fall is irrational noise: record 13.9% operating margin, AWS accelerating to 39.3%, and the stock at ~15x operating cash flow, its lowest since 2009.
calls.price_at_call: ~15x trailing operating cash flow vs 25.8x long-run median; conservative DCF implies 20%+ annual share-price compounding over 3 years (20% OCF growth, 17x multiple)
calls.base_case: AWS grows 40% in both 2027 and 2028 (~$392B revenue, ~$145B operating income at 37% margin); Q4 gives a cleaner comparison with advertising back to high-teens growth.
calls.bull_case: AI capex ROI proves out, the multiple re-expands toward 20x+ operating cash flow, and Amazon ends up with two $1T-revenue businesses (e-commerce and AWS).
calls.bear_case: Free-cash-flow burn (-$35B in the quarter, -$62B YTD) funded by debt ($115B raised YTD) stays unsustainable if AI build-out ROI disappoints; AI agents could disrupt the advertising business.

calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (prior BUY 12 Oct): same closing line as the Meta call — his focus is still going to be on buying more Amazon (and Meta) rather than adding Google, because those businesses offer a lot more value. Amazon's own earnings video is due tomorrow after the close; no Amazon-specific thesis or price is developed in this video.

Conditional buy at $200-$225, first explicit stance (prior tracked was UNCERTAIN): Amazon reports Thursday, AWS grew 37% last quarter and advertising is its highest-margin business, helping an expected ~80% earnings rise to $12.90 on ~15% revenue growth, but capex guided to $220bn has swung free cash flow from +$32bn in 2024 to -$11bn over the last year, which he calls the market's central AI fear. At 20x earnings / 3.5x sales he thinks analysts (average target $330) are overly bullish short term and he would be more comfortable buying at $200-$225.
calls.price_at_call: His buy zone $200-$225; 20x P/E, 3.5x sales; analyst average target $330 as stated
